title: Holographic zeros and poles from apparent singularities
abstract: We study general holographic fluctuation equations with apparent singularities, and the associated spectral functions. We consider the regime where an apparent singularity approaches the boundary, for which the near-boundary behavior of solutions can be determined via an inner/outer matching type of calculation. Depending on properties of the equation, we find that the merging of an apparent singularity with the boundary may generate either a zero or a pole for the corresponding spectral function. Our results also indicate that the recently introduced holographic product formula still applies in the presence of apparent singularities.
summary: This work analyzes holographic fluctuation equations containing apparent singularities to determine the resulting spectral properties. By studying the near-boundary behavior, the authors show that the singularity's merging with the boundary dictates whether the spectral function acquires a zero or a pole. This provides a general, powerful tool for calculating transport coefficients in strongly coupled quantum matter systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the merging of an apparent singularity with the boundary affects the spectral functions derived from holographic fluctuation equations.
main_result: The merging of the singularity can generate either a zero or a pole in the corresponding spectral function, and the holographic product formula remains applicable.
method: The analysis uses near-boundary matching techniques on second-order linear differential equations (fluctuation equations) derived from holographic setups.
model_or_system: The model is a holographic setup, relating bulk fluctuations in backgrounds like AdS black branes to boundary two-point functions ($ho$). The governing equations are reduced to Schrödinger-like forms with potentials that can exhibit apparent singularities.
key_observables: Spectral function $ho(\omega)$ and the two-point correlator $G_{12}(\omega, k_i)$.
important_parameters: The approach depends on classifying equations into $(−)$ and $(+)$ classes, and analyzing the limit where an apparent singularity approaches the boundary ($r^* 	o 0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the apparent nature of the singularity and relies on matching solutions between inner (near-boundary) and outer regions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the general holographic setting for spectral functions, details the near-boundary analysis using inner/outer matching, deduces general properties for zeros based on the singularity merging, and concludes with applications.
why_interesting: The connection between bulk singularities (apparent singularities) and the spectral properties (zeros/poles) of boundary correlators is a powerful tool for understanding transport and response functions in strongly interacting quantum systems modeled by holography.
